highLevelPlan: Resolve the one contradiction first: clarify decision #4 (PixelDiffer expect/actual) is overridden. ImageBitmap.readPixels(buffer, startX, startY, w, h, offset, stride) is a commonMain member (recon §5, proven by FakeFrameBitmap overriding it) and a region read IS startX/startY/w/h set to the annotation rect. The diff is IntArray arithmetic in commonMain with no seam. A separate, genuinely new fun-interface seam is still needed to READ frame.png off disk (BatchFileStore is write-only).

Read path (gap 1 + gap 2 together): add @Transaction @Query(... WHERE id = :id) to HistoryEntryDao, HistoryDataSource.getBatch(id), a BatchFileReader fun interface beside BatchFileStore, and HistoryRepository.get(batchId): SentBatchModel? that re-uses the EXISTING SentBatchModel write-path type as the read model (it already carries id/sentAtMs/deviceLabel/prompt/frameBytes/thumbPng/hierarchyXml/annotations). One new use case GetSentBatchUseCase + one UpdateBatchStatusUseCase (none exists; only ObserveHistory/RecordSentBatch ship).

Do NOT read crop-N.png at all. The full-res frame.png plus the stored rects is strictly more information than the crops, so the 0-based/1-based crop-index conflict (F-8 review finding F-8, FR-47) never arises on the read side and is confined to the follow-up envelope, where assembleEnvelope already numbers 1-based. FR-47 is satisfied by not having the problem.

Diff per annotation = three conjuncts, all computed from data the repo already produces: (a) node matched by snapTarget on BOTH sides, (b) F-5's measure() finding is GONE in the AFTER measurement, (c) the pixel region visibly changed above a tunable ratio. 'Fixed' requires all three; anything else is 'Still off' (closed AND-rule, AC-41 unmatched-node clause falls out of (a)).

The hierarchy half needs almost no new logic: F-5's findingOf IS the oracle. The design's own strings prove it — 'top Δ6dp → 0dp' is a TopMisalignment finding that went to zero (Fixed); 'height 24dp → 32dp · want 48dp' is a TouchTarget finding that moved but still fails (Still off). Only one new pure function is needed: a before→after label built on deltaLabel/plainValueLabel/displayDelta/SEPARATOR.

Keep every byte of diff arithmetic over IntArray so presentation-feature-mirror's Skiko-less desktopTest can run it; ImageBitmap only appears in a 10-line regionPixels(rect) edge function that clamps and calls readPixels.

Verify is a new MirrorStage.Verify case + a branch in MirrorStageContent's when + a condition in MirrorUiState.stage. The only RectifyWindow.kt edit is one extra parameter on the content lambda (it already widened 3→4 args for frozenHierarchy); the two bitmaps ride a new plain StateFlow<VerifyFrames?>, never reduced state.

Follow-up re-uses resolveAndSend() with one two-line addition: build a FrozenFrame over the freshly captured HeldFrame holding the still-off annotations renumbered 1..N, set the three current* flows, reduce, call resolveAndSend(), and have its success path consume a pendingFollowUpBatchId to write FollowUpSent. Crops come from the AFTER frame for free because assembleEnvelope crops the current frozen held bitmap.

Status writes happen last and only at terminal points: all-Fixed or Mark-all-as-verified → Verified; follow-up send succeeded → FollowUpSent on the ORIGINAL batch (the follow-up also records its own new Sent row, which is correct — a follow-up is itself verifiable). A mixed run with no user action writes nothing, which is what makes NFR-16's 'no partial status write' true by ordering rather than by a transaction.
data.proposedArchitecture:
One new pure package presentation-feature-mirror/core/verify/ (internal, Skiko-free, unit-tested), one new stage case, one new StateFlow, and a thin read path down the existing layer stack.

Data/domain (new, all small): HistoryEntryDao.@Transaction @Query findById → HistoryDataSource.getBatch(id): HistoryEntryWithAnnotations? → BatchFileReader (fun interface, suspend fun read(path: String): ByteArray?, java.io desktop impl, null-returning Android/iOS stand-ins, never throws) → HistoryRepositoryImpl.get(batchId): SentBatchModel? which fills frameBytes from framePath, hierarchyXml from hierarchyPath, annotations from the @Relation children (cropBytes left empty — unused), and reconstitutes the BEFORE HierarchySnapshotModel by feeding the stored XML through the EXISTING HierarchySnapshotMapper.toModel with HierarchyDumpStdout(dump = xml, density = ""). That mapper is already internal to data-repository-impl, which is exactly where the parse must happen (presentation must never import data-device-api). → GetSentBatchUseCase: Result<SentBatchModel> and UpdateBatchStatusUseCase: Optional, both plain resultLauncher wrappers.

The BEFORE snapshot comes back with densityDpi = 0 (the density stdout was never persisted — gap 4). Density for BOTH sides is therefore taken from the fresh AFTER dump; see the density decision.

Presentation (presentation-feature-mirror):
- core/verify/RegionPixels.kt — ImageBitmap.regionPixels(rect, frameSize): IntArray? — clamps the rect into the frame (a dragged annotation can overhang) and calls readPixels into a right-sized IntArray. The ONLY file in the feature that touches an ImageBitmap for diffing; deliberately untested because Skiko is absent from desktopTest.
- core/verify/RegionDiff.kt — internal fun changedRatio(before: IntArray, after: IntArray): Float. Pure, IntArray-in Float-out, no Compose types at all, fully unit-testable without Skiko.
- core/verify/VerifyThresholds.kt — the three tunable named constants with stated ceilings (see techStack).
- core/verify/VerifyVerdict.kt — internal fun verdictOf(matched, beforeFinding, afterFinding, changedRatio, regionPx): VerificationOutcome. Pure; the AND-rule lives here and nowhere else.
- core/verify/BeforeAfterFormat.kt — the single missing formatter, built on deltaLabel / plainValueLabel / displayDelta / SEPARATOR. No unit conversion is reimplemented.
- source/mirror/MirrorVerifyStage.kt — the composable: two MirrorFrameView columns (BEFORE neutral rects, AFTER verdict-coloured), the 300px Verification panel of VerificationRows, the four-step strip (StatusLine molecule), the footer actions, the ← Back to live chip.
- MirrorContract.kt — MirrorStage.Verify; VerifyUiState(batchId, deviceLabel, sentAtMs, recapturedAtMs, phase, rows, error); VerifyRow(index, comment, beforeRect, afterRect, resultLine, outcome) — all value-equal, no bitmaps; VerifyPhase { Loading, Recapturing, Diffing, Ready }; VerifyError { NotOnDisk, SizeMismatch, HierarchyUnusable, NoLiveSession, Disconnected }; intents SendFollowUp, MarkAllVerified, ExitVerify (VerifyBatch already exists).
- MirrorViewModel — verifyJob: Job? mirroring the dumpJob precedent; verifyFrames: MutableStateFlow<VerifyFrames?> (the 5th MirrorHost content arg); pendingFollowUpBatchId: String?.

The run, as one cancellable suspend function on verifyJob, every pixel step inside withContext(Dispatchers.Default):
1. Snapshot sessionDeviceId and currentHeld.value atomically. Null held ⇒ NoLiveSession (there is no one-shot capture use case; see decisions).
2. GetSentBatchUseCase(batchId). Null/failure ⇒ NotOnDisk (the stored path is a hint, never a guarantee).
3. decodeToImageBitmap() the stored frameBytes. Compare its IntSize with the live HeldFrame's. Disagree ⇒ SizeMismatch, abort BEFORE any per-annotation work (FR-46/AC-40). From here on there is exactly ONE IntSize and ONE density for both sides, which collapses the whole MeasureProjection landmine to a single check.
4. DumpHierarchyUseCase(deviceId) — the ~2.7 s cost; phase = Recapturing drives the visible progress state (NFR-15).
5. Project both snapshots against that one shared IntSize. A snapshot that is non-empty but projects to an EMPTY candidate list is a coordinate-space mismatch (the documented Pixel 8 984×2132-vs-1080×2400 display-override case) ⇒ HierarchyUnusable, abort. A snapshot that was empty to begin with is not an abort — it degrades per-annotation to NO_MATCH_NODE_ID and therefore to 'Still off' exactly as AC-41 requires.
6. Per annotation i (0-based history order): measure(rect, i+1, beforeNodes, size, dpi) and measure(rect, i+1, afterNodes, size, dpi); regionPixels on both bitmaps; changedRatio; verdictOf; beforeAfterLabel. Publish VerifyFrames(before, after) on the StateFlow and reduce VerifyUiState with the rows.
7. All rows Fixed ⇒ UpdateBatchStatusUseCase(batchId, Verified). Otherwise write nothing.

At every suspension point, if sessionDeviceId changed or went null ⇒ Disconnected, no status write, phase retryable (NFR-16/AC-44). The existing flatMapLatest(sessionDeviceId) teardown already cancels verifyJob for free.

components.name: HistoryEntryDao.findById
components.responsibility: @Transaction @Query("SELECT * FROM history_entry WHERE id = :id") returning HistoryEntryWithAnnotations?. The @Relation already carries the annotations; only the query is missing. Explicitly NOT ReadableDataSource.getById, which is Int-keyed and useless for String batch ids.

components.name: BatchFileReader
components.responsibility: New fun interface in data-repository-impl beside BatchFileStore: suspend fun read(path: String): ByteArray?. One abstract method so SAM conversion still works (adding read() to BatchFileStore would destroy its fun-interface-ness). java.io desktop impl; null-returning Android/iOS stand-ins; never throws. The only genuinely new seam in F-9.

components.name: HistoryRepository.get(batchId)
components.responsibility: Returns the EXISTING SentBatchModel (reused as the read model, not a new type) plus the BEFORE HierarchySnapshotModel parsed from the stored XML through the existing HierarchySnapshotMapper. Returns null when the row is absent or framePath/hierarchyPath is null or unreadable.

components.name: GetSentBatchUseCase / UpdateBatchStatusUseCase
components.responsibility: Two thin resultLauncher(errorMapper = Failure.Technical::Database) wrappers. Neither exists today — HistoryRepository.updateStatus has zero callers and no use case at all.

components.name: RegionDiff.changedRatio(before: IntArray, after: IntArray): Float
components.responsibility: The entire pixel metric, in one pure function over two IntArrays. No ImageBitmap, no Compose type, no seam — so it runs in the Skiko-less desktopTest. This is the single most important testability decision in the feature.

components.name: RegionPixels.regionPixels(bitmap, rect, frameSize): IntArray?
components.responsibility: The ImageBitmap edge: clamp the annotation rect into the frame (a drag can overhang), allocate w*h, call the commonMain readPixels(buffer, startX, startY, w, h, 0, w). Returns null for a degenerate rect. Ten lines, deliberately untested.

components.name: VerifyThresholds
components.responsibility: CHANNEL_NOISE_FLOOR, REGION_CHANGE_RATIO, MIN_REGION_PIXELS — three internal const vals in one file, each with a KDoc naming its ceiling and the tuning method, per NFR-17/MET-3. Not magic numbers scattered at call sites.

components.name: VerifyVerdict.verdictOf(...)
components.responsibility: The AND-rule in exactly one expression: matched && afterFinding == null && pixelEvidence. Returns the already-shipped VerificationOutcome enum (Fixed/StillOff) rather than inventing a parallel type.

components.name: BeforeAfterFormat.beforeAfterLabel(...)
components.responsibility: The one formatter the repo lacks: 'top ' + deltaLabel(before) + ' → ' + deltaLabel(after), and plainValueLabels joined by SEPARATOR for the touch-target shape. Built entirely on F-5's displayDelta/deltaLabel/plainValueLabel/SEPARATOR — zero unit conversion is reimplemented.

components.name: MirrorStage.Verify + MirrorStageContent branch
components.responsibility: One enum case, one when branch, one condition in the MirrorUiState.stage derivation (ordered before Frozen/Streaming). No new Destination, no second MirrorHost call site.

components.name: VerifyFrames + MirrorViewModel.verifyFrames StateFlow
components.responsibility: data class VerifyFrames(before: ImageBitmap, after: ImageBitmap) on a plain StateFlow, handed in as a 5th MirrorHost content arg. Honours Deviation 2 (pixels never enter reduced state) while delivering the two bitmaps the design needs.

components.name: MirrorVerifyStage composable
components.responsibility: Two 296×640 MirrorFrameView columns with per-annotation rect overlays (BEFORE neutral, AFTER verdict-coloured), the 300px Verification panel of VerificationRows, StatusLine for the four-step strip, footer AppButtons, and the ← Back to live chip wired to ExitVerify → ResumeLive + shellState.selectTab(History).

components.name: verifyJob + VerifyPhase
components.responsibility: Cancellation and progress, copied from the existing dumpJob precedent. Phase drives the in-progress UI (NFR-15) and makes the ~2.7 s dumpHierarchy legible instead of a dead window.

components.name: pendingFollowUpBatchId
components.responsibility: A plain nullable field set immediately before re-entering resolveAndSend(), consumed in its success path to write FollowUpSent on the ORIGINAL batch. This is the two-line amendment that makes 'reuse resolveAndSend unchanged' honest.

alternatives.title: No seam at all for pixel diffing — IntArray arithmetic in commonMain (RECOMMENDED, overrides clarify decision #4)
pros: readPixels(buffer, startX, startY, width, height, bufferOffset, stride) is a commonMain MEMBER of ImageBitmap — the recon proves it, because the existing FakeFrameBitmap overrides that exact signature. Setting startX/startY/width/height to the annotation rect IS the region read; there is nothing platform-specific left to abstract.
ThumbnailBitmap.kt already did a non-trivial commonMain pixel job (crop + scale + FilterQuality) with zero new seams. Direct in-repo precedent for exactly this.

Keeps the arithmetic over IntArray, which is the ONLY shape that survives the Skiko trap: presentation-feature-mirror's desktopTest has no Skiko native library, so any design that hides the diff behind a desktop-only implementation is untestable in the very module that owns it.
Honours the two strongest rules in the repo at once: 'prefer a fun interface over expect/actual' AND 'no interface with one implementation'.

Cannot crash on Android/iOS: it is integer arithmetic. The AS-29 null-stand-in concern is already satisfied upstream — BatchFileReader returns null there, so GetSentBatchUseCase returns null and Verify never reaches the diff.
cons: Contradicts a closed clarify decision, so it needs an explicit, recorded override (this document).
Loses the theoretical option of a future platform-accelerated differ — recoverable later for the cost of one extraction, and YAGNI until a profile says otherwise.
alternatives.tradeoffs: The clarify decision's premise was a question the input.md ambiguity list raised ('does raw pixel access exist cross-platform?') and the recon then answered: yes, in commonMain. Keeping the seam would add a module-crossing abstraction to protect against a platform difference that does not exist, and would simultaneously destroy unit-testability. Overriding is the smaller and safer change.

alternatives.title: fun interface PixelDiffer with a desktopMain implementation
pros: Matches the CropEncoder/BatchFileStore shape a reviewer will pattern-match for.
Keeps clarify decision #4's spirit (desktop-only, null stand-ins) with the repo's preferred seam kind rather than expect/actual.
cons: One interface, one implementation, no second caller — the exact shape the repo's own rules forbid.
Pushes the arithmetic into desktopMain, where desktopTest STILL has no Skiko. The seam buys nothing for testability and costs the ability to test the diff in commonTest.

CropEncoder exists because AWT ImageIO encoding genuinely has no commonMain equivalent; BatchFileStore exists because there is no okio/kotlinx-io in the catalog. Neither justification applies to integer subtraction.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Consistency-by-appearance against consistency-by-reason. The two existing seams exist for a concrete missing API; copying their shape where no API is missing is cargo cult.

alternatives.title: expect/actual PixelDiffer (clarify decision #4 as written)
pros: Literally what the confirmed survey says.
cons: The repo reserves expect/actual for DatabaseBuilder and SettingsProvider only, and documents the fun-interface preference explicitly.
Needs an actual in four source sets (android, iosArm64, iosSimulatorArm64, desktop) for code that is identical everywhere.
Inherits every con of the fun-interface option plus more files.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Strictly dominated. Recorded here only so the override is traceable.

alternatives.title: Pixel half as change-evidence: Fixed requires the region to have visibly CHANGED (RECOMMENDED)
pros: You cannot honestly claim 'Fixed' from pixels that never moved. An agent that did nothing produces an identical region, and this is the only rule that catches that.
Directly serves MET-3's worse failure direction — 'marked Fixed but the issue is still present' is the trust-destroying error for a verification tool.
Matches the design's own narrative: BEFORE is the buggy frame, three files were changed, the AFTER rects are coloured by what actually moved.
Region-scoped, so a status-bar clock or a blinking caret elsewhere on screen is invisible to it.
cons: An annotation that was already fine and that the agent correctly left alone reads 'Still off'. The user clears it with the already-specified 'Mark all as verified', and a false 'Still off' is the cheap error.
A full-region animation mid-flight (a scroll, a shimmer) registers as 'changed' and so removes the pixel objection — the layout half then carries the verdict alone.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Literal AC-24 prose ('no material difference → resolved') reads the other way, but the glossary's own MET-3 definition counts 'marked Fixed but still broken' as a false positive, so the prose is self-contradictory. Change-evidence is the reading that makes the metric achievable.

alternatives.title: Pixel half as similarity: Fixed when the region still looks the same as BEFORE (literal AC-24)
pros: Literal fidelity to the AC-24 sentence and to the glossary's 'below threshold → resolved'.
cons: An agent that does nothing at all gets every findings-free annotation marked Fixed. That is the single worst outcome the feature can produce.
Inverts the product meaning of the differentiator: the whole point is to detect whether the fix landed, and 'the pixels never moved' is evidence it did not.
Maximises exactly the false-positive class MET-3 names.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Buys literal AC compliance at the cost of the feature being wrong. If the orchestrator insists, AC-24's wording should be amended in plan rather than implemented as written.

alternatives.title: Pixel half advisory only — verdict from the hierarchy/measure half alone
pros: The design never displays a pixel percentage anywhere; every result string shown is a measurement delta.
Smallest possible implementation — the measure half needs almost no new code.
Zero false positives from animation, scrolling or antialiasing.
cons: Violates FR-41 and AC-23, both of which require the pixel-region diff to contribute to the verdict.
Blind to every defect with no geometry signature: wrong colour, wrong text, wrong icon, clipping, overlap — a large share of real UI bugs.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Tempting and genuinely lazy, but it deletes half of the stated differentiator. Keep the pixel half; keep it cheap.

alternatives.title: densityDpi from the fresh AFTER dump, no schema change (RECOMMENDED)
pros: Zero migration. database.md requires a @Database version bump AND a real Migration for a new column, and F-8's 'stayed at version 1' is explicitly flagged as a one-off that is NOT reusable.

Decisive point: a migration cannot retroactively supply density for rows already on disk. Every pre-migration batch would still need a live-density fallback, so the fallback must be built either way — building only the fallback is strictly less code for strictly the same coverage.
AS-2 pins Verify to the same device, so the density is the same physical constant unless the user ran `wm density` between send and verify.
FR-46 collapses both sides onto one IntSize anyway, so one density for both sides is coherent by construction.
Degrades honestly: densityDpi = 0 is already the repo-wide 'unknown' sentinel and PixelUnits labels everything raw px — the existing, tested behaviour.
cons: A deliberate mid-session density change silently relabels the BEFORE side in the new density. Unmeasurable in practice and strictly better than labelling everything px.
The stored side is not independently labellable, which is a real (and recorded) data gap.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Adding the column is the 'correct' data model and costs an entity field, a mapper field, a write-path change, a version bump, a hand-written Migration, a migration test — and still does not fix a single existing row. Classic correct-but-worthless.

alternatives.title: Add a densityDpi column to history_entry with a real Room migration
pros: Each batch carries its own density; the BEFORE side becomes independently labellable; the right long-term shape if dp labels ever need to be archival.
cons: Full migration ceremony per database.md; helps zero existing rows; the live-density fallback is still required for them; pure cost in v1.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Correct direction, wrong release. Record it as the upgrade path behind the fallback.

alternatives.title: Require an active mirror session on the device for Verify (RECOMMENDED)
pros: AS-1 asserts an on-demand capture pipeline exists without the live mirror running; the recon proves it does not — StartMirroringUseCase is stream-only and there is no one-shot capture use case.
The re-capture then costs nothing: one atomic currentHeld.value read, exactly how stageAnnotation already freezes a frame.
DumpHierarchyUseCase is already documented as safe to call during mirroring.
The failure mode is a clear, actionable error state ('Start mirroring this device, then Verify') rather than a wrong answer.
cons: Verify is not usable from a cold start, which reads as a product limitation on the History tab.
Falsifies AS-1 as written — must be recorded as a corrected assumption, not quietly ignored.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Building a one-shot screencap path (new adb invocation, new use case, new error surface, new tests) to avoid one precondition is a feature-sized detour inside an already-XL feature.

alternatives.title: Build a one-shot CaptureFrameUseCase so Verify works without a live session
pros: Makes AS-1 true; Verify becomes reachable from History at any time; the capture pipeline becomes reusable for later features.
cons: New adb path down through data-device, a new use case, new failures to surface, and it duplicates the streaming pipeline's decode path. Not asked for by any FR.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Right thing to build the day a second caller appears. Today there is none.

alternatives.title: Abort the whole run when a non-empty hierarchy projects to zero candidates (RECOMMENDED)
pros: projectMeasureNodes discards a snapshot whose root bounds disagree with the passed frame size — the documented Pixel 8 display-override case (984×2132 dump vs 1080×2400 panel, a 9.76% gap).
Without the guard the user gets N confident 'Still off' verdicts caused by a tooling mismatch, which is the most expensive possible lie from a verification tool.

Cleanly separable from AC-41: an EMPTY stored snapshot (no dump captured) still degrades per-annotation to NO_MATCH and therefore to 'Still off', exactly as AC-41 requires. Only non-empty-but-rejected aborts.
cons: One more error case to render and localise.
Verify becomes unavailable on display-override devices until measure mode itself is fixed — but it was never going to be correct there.
alternatives.tradeoffs: One extra VerifyError case against a whole class of silent wrong answers.

alternatives.title: Widen the MirrorHost content lambda with a 5th VerifyFrames? parameter (RECOMMENDED)
pros: The lambda has already widened once (3→4 args, for frozenHierarchy) — established precedent, not a new idea.
Exactly one call site to touch; a holder type means one new parameter rather than two.
Keeps both bitmaps out of reduced state (Deviation 2) and keeps the one-MirrorHost-call-site rule intact.
cons: Costs a ~2-line edit in RectifyWindow.kt, so the recon's 'needs no RectifyWindow.kt change' holds for the stage when but not for the lambda arity. Be honest about that in the plan.
A 5-arg content lambda is getting wide; a single MirrorFrames holder for all three bitmaps is the natural refactor if a sixth ever appears.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Two lines in one file against any scheme that smuggles bitmaps through state or a CompositionLocal.

alternatives.title: Follow-up re-stages ALL still-off annotations in one envelope, not one (RECOMMENDED)
pros: AC-42 says 'exactly the still-off annotations' (plural) and the design's footer literally reads 'Send follow-up · N' where N is the still-off count.
The recon's 'exactly one StagedAnnotation' is just the N=1 case of the same code.
One send, one envelope, one agent round trip — fewer interruptions than N sends.
cons: Renumbering 1..N must be done carefully so the follow-up's indices are envelope-correct (1-based) while the diff loop iterated history's 0-based indices — which is the whole of FR-47, confined to this one map call.
alternatives.tradeoffs: None worth the words. FR-21's singular phrasing is the degenerate case.

exceptions: GetSentBatchUseCase returns Failure.Logic.NotFound when the row is missing, and null-ish NotFound when framePath/hierarchyPath is null or unreadable — a stored path is documented as a hint, never a guarantee (F-8 KDoc). The UI renders VerifyError.NotOnDisk, not a crash.
BatchFileReader never throws. Unreadable, missing, permission-denied, truncated → null. Same contract as BatchFileStore.write, enforced by the same reasoning.
decodeToImageBitmap() on corrupt stored bytes: wrapped, null on failure, → VerifyError.NotOnDisk. Null-on-failure is universal in this repo; a failed image never fails the operation.
FR-46/AC-40 frame-size mismatch: abort BEFORE any per-annotation work. Checked once against the decoded frame.png size vs the live HeldFrame size, not per annotation.
Non-empty snapshot projecting to zero candidates (display-override coordinate-space mismatch) → VerifyError.HierarchyUnusable, abort. Distinct from an empty snapshot, which degrades per-annotation.

Device disconnect at any suspension point (sessionDeviceId changed or null) → VerifyError.Disconnected, no status write, retryable. The existing flatMapLatest(sessionDeviceId) teardown cancels verifyJob for free (AC-44/NFR-16).
DumpHierarchyUseCase failure → VerifyError.HierarchyUnusable rather than silently diffing pixels alone; the AND-rule requires both halves and a one-legged verdict would be a lie.
An annotation rect that overhangs the frame (a drag past the edge) is clamped before readPixels; a rect that clamps to zero area skips the pixel half and falls back to the hierarchy half alone.

'Mark all as verified' bypasses every diff and writes Verified unconditionally (FR-44) — including while a run is still in progress, in which case it cancels verifyJob first so a late completion cannot overwrite the user's override.
A follow-up send that fails (handoff.publish failure) leaves the ORIGINAL batch status untouched; FollowUpSent is written only after resolveAndSend reaches its success point.
edgeCases: Antialiasing, subpixel text rendering and gamma wobble — absorbed by CHANNEL_NOISE_FLOOR; they move single channels by a few units, well under the floor.
A blinking text caret inside an annotated field: a 2×30 px caret inside a 200×60 px region is 0.5% of the area, under REGION_CHANGE_RATIO. Sized deliberately so.
A status-bar clock ticking: only visible if the user annotated the status bar. The diff is region-scoped, not whole-screen — which is exactly why the PRD insists on per-region.

A scroll or an animation mid-flight: the region reads 'changed', so the pixel conjunct passes and the measure half carries the verdict alone. Degrades to the hierarchy answer rather than to a wrong answer.
An agent that changed nothing: identical region ⇒ pixel conjunct fails ⇒ 'Still off'. The headline case the change-evidence semantics exist to catch.
An annotation that was already correct and was correctly left alone: reads 'Still off'. Cleared by 'Mark all as verified'. The cheap error, taken knowingly.
Two annotations overlapping the same node: both snap to the same MeasureNode and get the same layout verdict but different pixel regions. Correct and intended.
Zero annotations on the batch: Verify shows an empty Verification panel and 'Mark all as verified' is the only sensible action. Guard N=0 so 'Send follow-up · 0' is disabled.
Orientation change between send and verify: caught by FR-46's size check (w/h swap is a size mismatch).
Device density changed via `wm density` between send and verify: undetectable in v1 (density is not persisted). Recorded as a gap, not handled.
The follow-up send records its OWN new history row with status Sent while the original flips to FollowUpSent. Intended: a follow-up is itself verifiable, which is how the loop actually closes.

Verify clicked on a row whose framePath is null (disk write failed at send time): the recon's suggested honest gate. Keep the button rendered per FR-37/AC-39 and fail with NotOnDisk, rather than reintroducing a status-shaped gate that AC-39 just deleted.
Verify clicked while a previous verify is still running: cancel verifyJob and start the new one (flatMapLatest semantics by hand).

Verify clicked for a batch sent from a DIFFERENT device than the one currently mirrored: v1 does not attempt to match serials (deviceLabel is a label, not a serial). The run uses the live device and the header shows the stored label; out of scope per the clarify, but worth one line in the UI.
Very small annotation regions (a 6×6 icon): below MIN_REGION_PIXELS the ratio is statistically meaningless, so the pixel conjunct is skipped and the hierarchy half decides alone.
implementationSteps: 1. Data read path: HistoryEntryDao.findById (@Transaction @Query by String id) + HistoryDataSource.getBatch + DAO desktopTest for present/absent/with-children.
2. BatchFileReader fun interface + java.io desktop impl + Android/iOS null stand-ins + Koin registration beside BatchFileStore.

3. HistoryRepositoryImpl.get(batchId): assemble the existing SentBatchModel from the @Relation plus BatchFileReader bytes, and reconstitute the BEFORE HierarchySnapshotModel via the existing HierarchySnapshotMapper.toModel(HierarchyDumpStdout(xml, "")). commonTest with a fake data source and a fake reader.
4. GetSentBatchUseCase + UpdateBatchStatusUseCase (api + impl + Koin, appended within the layer group — never reordered).

5. core/verify/RegionDiff.kt + VerifyThresholds.kt + VerifyVerdict.kt + BeforeAfterFormat.kt — all pure, all commonTest-covered, no Skiko, no Compose types. This is the step that proves the no-seam decision.
6. core/verify/RegionPixels.kt — the clamp + readPixels edge. No test (Skiko absent); kept to ~10 lines precisely because it cannot be tested.
7. MirrorContract.kt: MirrorStage.Verify, VerifyUiState/VerifyRow/VerifyPhase/VerifyError, SendFollowUp/MarkAllVerified/ExitVerify intents, and the stage-derivation condition (ordered before Frozen).

8. MirrorViewModel.verifyBatch: replace the log.i stub with the seven-step run on verifyJob, every pixel step under withContext(Dispatchers.Default), device-identity re-checked at each suspension point. ViewModel tests with fakes for the new use cases (MirrorFakes.kt already pins Orbit's event-loop dispatcher).
9. verifyFrames StateFlow + 5th MirrorHost content arg + the one RectifyWindow.kt call-site edit.
10. MirrorVerifyStage composable + MirrorStageContent branch + strings (mirror_verify_*) + light/dark @Preview pair per the preview convention.

11. Remove the BatchStatusModel.Fixed gate at MirrorHistoryTab.kt:179 and the three collateral comments the recon lists (MirrorHistoryTab.kt:240 preview KDoc, strings.xml:182, MirrorContract.kt:490-500 KDoc).

12. Follow-up path: build the FrozenFrame over the fresh HeldFrame with still-off annotations renumbered 1..N, set the three current* flows, reduce, set pendingFollowUpBatchId, call resolveAndSend(); consume pendingFollowUpBatchId in its success path to write FollowUpSent.
13. Mark-all-as-verified + the all-Fixed automatic path → UpdateBatchStatusUseCase(Verified).
14. Cross-target build (./gradlew :presentation-feature-mirror:build) — commonTest compiles for iosArm64 and backtick names must contain no comma or colon.
gaps: AS-1 IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. There is no one-shot capture use case; StartMirroringUseCase is stream-only. v1 requires an active mirror session on the device and fails with VerifyError.NoLiveSession otherwise. This correction must land in the plan, not be papered over.

densityDpi is not persisted and cannot be recovered for any historical batch. Density for both sides comes from the fresh AFTER dump. A schema column would help only batches recorded after the migration, so the fallback is needed regardless.

MET-3 (<5% false positives) is unmeasurable in v1: no golden before/after dataset, no Compose UI-test harness, no way to label ground truth. Thresholds ship as named constants with stated ceilings, tuned by manual spot-check (NFR-17). The upgrade path is a small corpus of real before/after frame pairs with hand-labelled verdicts under presentation-feature-mirror/src/commonTest/resources, replayed by one parameterised test.

No temporal stabilisation of the AFTER frame. A single currentHeld.value read can land mid-animation. The cheap upgrade (sample two frames ~250 ms apart and require the region to agree) is deliberately NOT in v1; add it if spot-checks show animation flakiness.

The batch's originating device is stored only as a human deviceLabel, not a serial, so Verify cannot assert AS-2 — it uses whatever device is currently mirrored. A deviceId column would fix it; out of scope per the clarify.

No result string exists for an annotation with no measure finding on either side (the design's 'placeholder fits · no clipping' is prototype copy with no computable source). v1 falls back to a plainValueLabel size line; the design's phrasing cannot be reproduced honestly.

AGENT CHANGES panel and the step strip's 'Agent fixed · 3 files' label have no data source (AnnotationEnvelope carries no file-level metadata and there is no git/MCP reverse channel). Panel cut per the closed decision; the step strip ships with that step as a static, countless label.
No Compose UI-test harness exists, so the Verify stage is covered by @Preview pairs only — same ceiling every other screen in this repo lives with.

The follow-up envelope re-sends the original comment verbatim; the agent gets no explicit 'this is attempt 2, here is what is still wrong' framing. One promptOverride line would add it; deferred as an open decision.
F-8 tech debt F-4 (observeAll has no LIMIT) is untouched by F-9 and the new findById must not copy that pattern — it reads exactly one row by primary key.

risks.text: Threshold tuning is unvalidated (MET-3). The constants are a first guess from reasoning about antialiasing, caret and scroll cases, not from measurement.
risks.mitigation: Three named constants in one file with KDoc ceilings; 'Mark all as verified' is always available as the human override; recorded as unverified-in-v1 per NFR-17; golden-corpus upgrade path written down in gaps.

risks.text: A display-override device (the documented Pixel 8 984×2132 vs 1080×2400 case) makes projectMeasureNodes discard the hierarchy and would otherwise produce N confident, wrong 'Still off' verdicts.
risks.mitigation: Explicit non-empty-but-rejected check on BOTH sides → VerifyError.HierarchyUnusable, abort before any verdict. Kept distinct from the empty-snapshot case so AC-41 still behaves.

risks.text: The Skiko trap: if any diff code drifts into an ImageBitmap-typed helper, the feature's own tests stop compiling or start throwing LibraryLoadException.
risks.mitigation: Exactly one file (RegionPixels.kt, ~10 lines) is allowed to mention ImageBitmap; RegionDiff takes IntArrays. Enforced by a KDoc note on both files and by the tests themselves, which never construct a bitmap.

risks.text: dumpHierarchy costs ~2.7 s and N region diffs follow, so a naive implementation reads as a frozen window.
risks.mitigation: VerifyPhase drives a visible progress state (NFR-15); all work on Dispatchers.Default off the intent context; verifyJob cancellable from ExitVerify, a new Verify, or a device change.

risks.text: Reusing resolveAndSend() is advertised as 'unchanged' but needs a pendingFollowUpBatchId hook in its success path; a sloppy edit could make every normal send try to write FollowUpSent.
risks.mitigation: Nullable field, null-checked, cleared in a finally; one ViewModel test asserting a plain send writes no status.

risks.text: The 0-based (history) vs 1-based (envelope) crop index could resurface when renumbering the follow-up annotations.
risks.mitigation: Never read crop-N.png at all, so there is only one conversion point: the mapIndexed that builds StagedAnnotation(index = i + 1). One test over a 2-of-3 still-off selection.

risks.text: Change-evidence semantics contradict the literal wording of AC-24, so a reviewer may flag the implementation as non-compliant.
risks.mitigation: Carried as survey question #2 with the reasoning recorded; if confirmed, AC-24's wording is amended in the plan rather than silently diverged from.

risks.text: Verify requiring a live mirror session may read as a bug on the History tab ('I clicked Verify and got an error').
risks.mitigation: A specific, actionable error state naming the device to start mirroring — not a generic failure. AS-1 corrected explicitly in the plan.

risks.text: Scope creep: F-9 touches data, domain, repository, presentation and the shell call site at once.
risks.mitigation: The 14 implementation steps are ordered so steps 1-6 are pure and independently testable before any UI exists; the read path (1-4) is mergeable on its own.

readyMadeSolutions.name: VerificationRow + VerificationOutcome
readyMadeSolutions.fit: Done and shipped: GlyphBadge ✓/! + title + mono delta + the outcome word in Theme.color.sentFixed / warnStillOff. Its own @Preview already uses the design's exact strings. F-9 only feeds it, and resolves outcomeLabel from strings.xml at the call site per localisation.md. Reuse VerificationOutcome as the verdict type — do not define a parallel enum.

readyMadeSolutions.name: Theme.color.sentFixed / warnStillOff

readyMadeSolutions.name: F-5 core/measure toolkit

Internal and in-module — reuse in place, never copy out. Only beforeAfterLabel is missing.

readyMadeSolutions.name: ThumbnailBitmap.cropAndScale

techStack.choice: ImageBitmap.readPixels(IntArray, startX, startY, w, h, 0, w) in commonMain, behind a ~10-line clamping helper
techStack.reason: Already cross-platform; a region read is just the rect as arguments. No seam, no dependency, no actual (overrides clarify decision #4).

techStack.choice: Per-pixel Chebyshev distance in RGB: changed(p) = max(|Δr|, |Δg|, |Δb|) > CHANNEL_NOISE_FLOOR; changedRatio = changedCount / n. Integer-only, one pass, alpha ignored (screenshots are opaque).
techStack.reason: Per-channel max catches a chroma-only change (a red→green button at equal luma) that a luma metric would miss, at the same cost. Integer arithmetic keeps it allocation-free and exactly reproducible in tests. SSIM/perceptual hashing would need a dependency and a float pipeline to answer a yes/no question.

techStack.choice: CHANNEL_NOISE_FLOOR = 10 (of 255), REGION_CHANGE_RATIO = 0.02f, MIN_REGION_PIXELS = 64 — three internal consts in VerifyThresholds.kt, each KDoc'd with its ceiling
techStack.reason: Floor 10 absorbs antialiasing, subpixel text and gamma wobble. 2% of area absorbs a blinking caret (a 2×30 caret in a 200×60 region is 0.5%) while a real content change is far larger. 64 px is the floor below which the ratio is statistically meaningless and the hierarchy half decides alone. Named, co-located and documented as tunable per NFR-17/MET-3, never inlined.

techStack.choice: Fixed ⇔ nodeMatched && afterFinding == null && (regionPx < MIN_REGION_PIXELS || changedRatio > REGION_CHANGE_RATIO). Anything else is StillOff.
techStack.reason: The closed AND-rule, expressed as three conjuncts. The middle one is F-5's own findingOf acting as the oracle — which is literally what the design's result strings show ('top Δ6dp → 0dp' = finding gone; 'height 24dp → 32dp · want 48dp' = finding remains). The first conjunct makes AC-41 fall out rather than be special-cased. ponytail ceiling: a NEW unrelated finding in AFTER also reads Still off — accepted, it is a regression and deserves the flag.

techStack.choice: fun interface BatchFileReader { suspend fun read(path: String): ByteArray? } in data-repository-impl, java.io desktop impl, null stand-ins
techStack.reason: This is the gap that is real: BatchFileStore is write-only and there is no okio/kotlinx-io in the catalog. One abstract method keeps it a fun interface; adding read() to BatchFileStore would not.

techStack.choice: Reuse the existing SentBatchModel as the read-path type (cropBytes left empty, which nothing consumes)
techStack.reason: It already carries every field the verify run needs. A parallel VerifyBatchModel would be a new type for the same data.
Same parse the live path uses, same fallbacks, and it keeps data-device-api out of presentation. Density comes back 0, which is exactly why the live-dump density decision exists.

techStack.choice: Take densityDpi from the fresh AFTER dump for both sides; no schema change, no migration
techStack.reason: A migration cannot retroactively supply density for rows already on disk, so the live fallback is required either way. 0 remains the repo's honest 'label in px' sentinel.

techStack.choice: data class VerifyFrames(before, after) on a plain StateFlow, handed in as a 5th MirrorHost content arg
techStack.reason: Honours Deviation 2 (pixels never enter reduced state) and the one-call-site rule; the lambda already widened once for frozenHierarchy.

techStack.choice: verifyJob: Job?, all decode/diff under withContext(Dispatchers.Default), device identity re-checked at each suspension point, VerifyPhase in reduced state
techStack.reason: The dumpJob precedent, NFR-15's visible progress, and NFR-16's clean abort, all from machinery that already exists.

techStack.choice: commonTest over IntArrays and pure functions only; no bitmap is ever constructed; no new test dependency
techStack.reason: presentation-feature-mirror's desktopTest has no Skiko, so ImageBitmap(w, h) throws there. Backtick test names must avoid commas and colons to survive compileTestKotlinIosArm64.

openDecisions.decision: Does the follow-up envelope reframe the comment for the agent ('still off after your fix: …') or re-send it verbatim?
options: Verbatim comment, no prompt change
Prefix each re-staged comment with a follow-up marker
Set promptOverride to a follow-up-specific prompt
openDecisions.recommendation: Verbatim in v1. Prefixing touches localisation and the payload preview's token estimate for a wording improvement nobody has asked for; promptOverride is already user-editable if they want it.

openDecisions.decision: Should the Verify button additionally be hidden/disabled when entry.framePath == null?
options: Always render (FR-37/AC-39 literal), fail with NotOnDisk
Render but disable when framePath is null
Hide when framePath is null
openDecisions.recommendation: Always render, fail with a specific error. AC-39 just deleted a status-shaped gate; adding a different gate in the same commit invites the same dead-affordance bug from the other direction. Disabling is a reasonable second choice.

openDecisions.decision: Where does the four-step strip's 'Agent fixed · N files' step get its count?
options: Static label with no count (no data source)
Omit the step entirely, three-step strip
Fabricate from annotation count
openDecisions.recommendation: Static label without a count. Omitting the step breaks the loop narrative the design calls its clearest statement; fabricating a number in a verification tool is the one thing that must never happen.

openDecisions.decision: Does an all-Fixed run write Verified automatically, or wait for the user?
options: Automatic on all-Fixed (AC-43 literal)
Always require an explicit click
openDecisions.recommendation: Automatic, per AC-43. 'Mark all as verified' remains the override for the mixed case.

openDecisions.decision: Should the two frame columns scale differently from the live stage (the design fixes them at 296×640)?
options: Reuse MirrorFrameView's aspect-correct sizing within a 296×640 box
Hard-code 296×640 and letterbox
Hard-code and stretch
openDecisions.recommendation: Aspect-correct within the box. Stretching a frame in a pixel-verification tool misrepresents the thing being verified.

survey.question: Clarify decision #4 chose a desktop-only PixelDiffer expect/actual seam, but the recon proves ImageBitmap.readPixels(buffer, startX, startY, w, h, offset, stride) is a commonMain member and that a region read is just the rect as arguments. How should the pixel diff be implemented?
options: No seam — pure IntArray arithmetic in commonMain, with a ~10-line readPixels edge function (overrides decision #4)
fun interface PixelDiffer with a desktopMain implementation and null-returning stand-ins
expect/actual PixelDiffer exactly as decision #4 states
survey.answer: No seam — pure IntArray arithmetic in commonMain, with a ~10-line readPixels edge function (overrides decision #4)
survey.rationale: Decision #4 answered an ambiguity ('does raw pixel access exist cross-platform?') that the recon then resolved: it does, in commonMain, proven by FakeFrameBitmap overriding that exact signature, and ThumbnailBitmap.kt already does non-trivial commonMain pixel work with zero seams. A seam here would be an interface with one implementation (forbidden by the repo's own rules), would add nothing for Android/iOS safety (integer arithmetic cannot crash, and BatchFileReader already returns null there so Verify never reaches the diff), and — decisively — would push the arithmetic into desktopMain where desktopTest STILL has no Skiko, destroying unit-testability for no gain. A separate fun-interface seam IS still needed to read frame.png off disk; that gap is real and is not this one.

survey.question: AC-24 says 'no material difference → resolved', which literally means an unchanged region counts as Fixed — so an agent that did nothing would be reported as having fixed the bug. Which pixel semantics should the verdict use?
options: Change-evidence: Fixed requires the region to have visibly CHANGED (plus the layout finding to be gone)
Similarity: Fixed when the region still matches BEFORE within threshold (AC-24 as literally worded)
Advisory: the pixel ratio is displayed but the verdict comes from the hierarchy half alone
survey.answer: Change-evidence: Fixed requires the region to have visibly CHANGED (plus the layout finding to be gone)
survey.rationale: You cannot honestly claim 'Fixed' from pixels that never moved, and MET-3's own glossary counts 'marked Fixed but the issue is still present' as a false positive — which the literal reading maximises. Change-evidence is region-scoped so a clock or caret elsewhere is invisible to it, and under the closed AND-rule the layout half still carries correctness. The advisory option is tempting (the design never displays a pixel percentage) but deletes half of FR-41/AC-23 and goes blind to every defect with no geometry signature: colour, text, icon, clipping, overlap. If this is confirmed, AC-24's wording should be amended in the plan rather than quietly diverged from.

survey.question: densityDpi was never persisted, so the stored BEFORE side re-parses with densityDpi = 0 (labels in raw px). How should dp labels be produced?
options: Take density from the fresh AFTER dump and apply it to both sides; no schema change
Add a densityDpi column to history_entry with a @Database version bump and a hand-written Migration
Label everything in raw px whenever the stored side has no density
survey.answer: Take density from the fresh AFTER dump and apply it to both sides; no schema change
survey.rationale: A migration cannot retroactively supply density for rows already on disk, so the live-density fallback has to be built either way — building only the fallback is strictly less code for strictly the same coverage. database.md also requires a real Migration (F-8's 'stayed at version 1' is explicitly flagged as non-reusable), and AS-2 already pins Verify to the same device, whose density is the same physical constant. FR-46 collapses both sides onto one frame size anyway, so one density for both is coherent. Raw px everywhere would contradict FR-40's 'same format as live measure-mode'. The column stays recorded as the upgrade path.

survey.question: AS-1 assumes an on-demand capture pipeline exists without the live mirror running, but the recon shows StartMirroringUseCase is stream-only with no one-shot capture use case. How should Verify obtain the AFTER frame?
options: Require an active mirror session on the device; read currentHeld.value atomically and fail with a clear 'start mirroring first' error otherwise
Build a new one-shot CaptureFrameUseCase so Verify works from a cold History tab
Fall back to the stored thumbnail when no session is live
survey.answer: Require an active mirror session on the device; read currentHeld.value atomically and fail with a clear 'start mirroring first' error otherwise
survey.rationale: The re-capture then costs nothing — one atomic currentHeld.value read, exactly how stageAnnotation already freezes a frame — and DumpHierarchyUseCase is already documented as safe during mirroring. Building a one-shot adb capture path is a feature-sized detour inside an already-XL feature, with no second caller to justify it. The thumbnail option is excluded outright by AC-45. AS-1 must be recorded as corrected in the plan rather than silently ignored.

survey.question: projectMeasureNodes discards an entire hierarchy whose root bounds disagree with the frame size (the documented Pixel 8 984×2132-vs-1080×2400 display-override case). What should happen when a stored or fresh hierarchy is non-empty but projects to zero candidates?
options: Abort the run with a distinct 'hierarchy does not match the frame' error, before any verdict is produced
Let it degrade per-annotation to no-match, producing N 'Still off' verdicts (AC-41 applied literally)
Fall back to a pixel-only verdict for that run
survey.answer: Abort the run with a distinct 'hierarchy does not match the frame' error, before any verdict is produced
survey.rationale: N confident 'Still off' verdicts caused by a coordinate-space mismatch is the most expensive lie a verification tool can tell, and it would push the user into a pointless follow-up send. AC-41's unmatched-node clause is still honoured exactly where it belongs: an EMPTY stored snapshot (no dump captured) still degrades per-annotation to NO_MATCH and therefore 'Still off'. Only non-empty-but-rejected aborts, which is a tooling problem, not a per-annotation outcome. The pixel-only fallback would silently break the closed AND-rule.

survey.question: MirrorHost hands the content lambda one bitmap and the Verify stage needs two (BEFORE + AFTER), while pixels must never enter reduced state and there must stay exactly one MirrorHost call site. How are both bitmaps delivered?
options: A new plain StateFlow<VerifyFrames?> handed in as a 5th content-lambda argument (one ~2-line RectifyWindow.kt edit)
Bundle frame + frozenFrame + verify frames into one MirrorFrames holder and keep the lambda at 4 args
Put the two ImageBitmaps in MirrorUiState, extending the audited history exception
survey.answer: A new plain StateFlow<VerifyFrames?> handed in as a 5th content-lambda argument (one ~2-line RectifyWindow.kt edit)
survey.rationale: The content lambda already widened once (3→4 args, for frozenHierarchy), so this is the established pattern and there is exactly one call site to touch. A holder type means one new parameter rather than two. Note honestly that this does cost a small RectifyWindow.kt edit — the recon's 'no RectifyWindow.kt change' holds for the stage when-branch but not for the lambda arity. Refactoring all three bitmaps into one holder is a bigger diff across unrelated call paths for a cosmetic win; putting bitmaps in reduced state is forbidden by Deviation 2 and would make identity-compared types defeat deduplication.
